This application coming on admission this day, th e court pass  following:
 ORDER 1.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner/complainant for quashing of FIR and further proceedings conducted in Crime No.51/2014, registered against respondents No.2 to 5 at Police Station Raoji Bazar, District Indore for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the IPC in light of compromise between the parties.

3. During pendency of the petition, both the parties have arrived at a compromise and have filed the same before this Court bearing IA No.558/2024 and I.A.No.560/2024 i.e. applications under Section 320(2) and 320 of Cr.P.C. for permission to compromise and also for recording the compromise.
4. Complete record of the case has been sent to the Principal Registrar of this Court for verification of the compromise and the parties were directed to appear before him.

On verification, the Principal Registrar has certified that the parties have entered into a compromise without any threat,
inducement and coercion from either side.

The complainant has admitted before the Principal Registrar that she has amicably has settled her dispute with the respondents No.2 to 5 and admitted that they have voluntarily entered into compromise.
5. It is submitted that the matter pertains to offence registered against the respondents No.2 to 5 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the IPC.
Now the parties have amicably settled the matter and the petitioner / complainant has no more grievance against the respondents No.2 to 5.

6. In the matter of B.S. Joshi vs. State of Haryana and Anr. reported in 2003 (4) SCC 675 the Apex Court has held that Section 320 of Cr.P.C. does not limit or affect inherent powers of High Court granted under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and in cases of matrimonial disputes if the application is filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. for quashing criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint, the same can be quashed. Hon'ble the Apex Court has reiterated the view in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab &
Arn. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Narinder Singh & Ors v. State of Punjab & Ors (2014) 6 SCC 466, Rajiv Saxena & Ors. vs. State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr. (2012) 3 SCC (Cri.) 327 and Yogendra Yadav & Ors. Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr. (2014) 9 SCC 653.

sentences.text: Looking to the nature of the dispute and the fact that the dispute has been amicably settled between the respondents No.2 to 5 and the complainant is not having any grievance with the respondents No.2 to 5, I find that the petition needs to be allowed and it is hereby allowed.

FIR bearing Crime No.51/2014 registered at Police Station Raoji Bazar District Indore under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B and 34 of the IPC and the proceedings pending in Sessions Trial No.462/2014 against the present respondents No.2 to 5 is hereby quashed.
8.
